Extended Kalman filter localization

Source: R/localization.R
robot_ekf.Rd

robot_ekf() creates a filter for the planar pose with mean mean and covariance cov. ekf_predict() propagates through the exact unicycle motion model with control noise covariance Q on c(v, omega), using the analytic Jacobians of unicycle_step(). ekf_update() fuses range-bearing measurements of known landmarks with covariance R, wrapping the bearing innovation and using the Joseph form so the covariance stays symmetric positive semidefinite. The heading estimate is wrapped after each step. Filters are immutable; each step returns a new filter.

robot_ekf(mean, cov, landmarks, Q, R)

ekf_predict(filter, control, dt)

ekf_update(filter, measurements)

Arguments

mean

Initial pose estimate.

cov

Initial 3 by 3 covariance.

landmarks

Matrix of landmark positions with row names as ids.

Q

Control noise covariance (2 by 2).

R

Measurement noise covariance (2 by 2).

filter

A robot_ekf.

control

c(v, omega).

dt

Duration (s).

measurements

A data frame as returned by landmark_measurements().

Value

A robot_ekf. ekf_update() also records the normalized innovation squared in nis.

Examples

L <- rbind(a = c(2, 0), b = c(0, 2))
f <- robot_ekf(c(0, 0, 0), diag(0.1, 3), L, Q = diag(c(0.01, 0.01)),
               R = diag(c(0.01, 0.001)))
f <- ekf_predict(f, c(1, 0), 0.1)
f <- ekf_update(f, landmark_measurements(c(0.1, 0, 0), L))
f$mean
#>     x     y theta 
#>   0.1   0.0   0.0
